title: CRIP Academic Poster Figure Inventory & Manifest

figures.title: U-Net Segmentation Dice Similarity by Structure
figures.description: Multi-class Sørensen-Dice similarity coefficient distributions for LV cavity, RV cavity, and myocardium on 20 held-out ACDC test scans (4 DCM, 4 HCM, 4 MINF, 4 NOR, 4 RV).

figures.title: 95th-Percentile Hausdorff Distance by Structure
figures.description: Spatial contour boundary distance error (HD95 in millimeters) across cardiac chambers at End-Diastole on 20 held-out ACDC test scans (4 DCM, 4 HCM, 4 MINF, 4 NOR, 4 RV).

figures.title: Predicted vs. Reference LVEF Scatter Plot
figures.description: Correlation and agreement between 2D U-Net predicted LVEF and expert ground-truth annotations with y=x identity line and SCMR 5% envelope (20 held-out test scans: 4 DCM, 4 HCM, 4 MINF, 4 NOR, 4 RV).

figures.title: Bland-Altman Agreement: LVEF
figures.description: Bland-Altman difference plot for Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction showing mean bias (-0.55 %-pts), 95% limits of agreement [-10.53, +9.43], and 95% confidence intervals on 20 held-out ACDC test scans (4 DCM, 4 HCM, 4 MINF, 4 NOR, 4 RV).

figures.title: Bland-Altman Agreement: LVEDV
figures.description: Bland-Altman difference plot for Left Ventricular End-Diastolic Volume showing mean bias (+2.13 mL) and limits of agreement [-15.73, +19.99] mL on 20 held-out ACDC test scans (4 DCM, 4 HCM, 4 MINF, 4 NOR, 4 RV).

figures.title: Bland-Altman Agreement: LVESV
figures.description: Bland-Altman difference plot for Left Ventricular End-Systolic Volume showing mean bias (+2.35 mL) and limits of agreement [-13.07, +17.77] mL on 20 held-out ACDC test scans (4 DCM, 4 HCM, 4 MINF, 4 NOR, 4 RV).

figures.title: Recovery Prediction: ROC Comparison
figures.description: Receiver Operating Characteristic curves comparing Logistic Regression (AUC = 0.9565) against Random Forest (AUC = 0.9310) on synthetic test data.

figures.title: Recovery Prediction: Reliability Calibration
figures.description: Reliability calibration curves evaluating predicted probability accuracy against observed event frequencies for Logistic Regression and Random Forest.
